fria.note: This block decides only whether the Article 27(1) FRIA obligation applies to the deployer. Conducting the assessment itself (the content elements of Article 27(1) points (a) to (f) and the Article 27(5) template) is out of scope here.
rationale: the system is classified minimal_or_none; Article 27(1) applies only to high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)
rule minimal: all prohibition-relevant AND Annex III high-risk flags known false, no Annex III category matched, no Article 50 transparency flag set

envelope.non_legal_advice_notice: TERE4AI provides engineering and documentation support. It does not certify EU AI Act compliance and does not replace legal review, conformity assessment, or competent-authority interpretation.

features.description: SpamGuard is a machine-learning email filter deployed by a 20-person company for its own shared inboxes. It classifies incoming email as ham, spam, or phishing using message text and metadata, moves likely spam to a retrievable quarantine folder, and flags suspected phishing links for the IT admin. It never blocks, deletes, or answers mail on its own; employees read their own mail and know the filter exists.
purposes: classify incoming email as ham, spam, or phishing
flag suspected phishing links for the IT admin
